Santa Biblia — Reina Valera 1909, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/spaRV1909/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/spaRV1909/copyright.htm):
> The Holy Bible in Spanish, Reina Valera translation of 1909
> Public Domain
> Language: Español (Spanish)
> Dialect: Castellano 1909
> Translation by: Reina y Valera
> Dominio Público
> 2013-12-13

What was found: eBible.org's text is the Reina-Valera revision called "1909". Its words match the edition printed in Madrid with the title-page date 1911: "La Santa Biblia que contiene los sagrados libros del Antiguo y Nuevo Testamento. Antigua versión de Cipriano de Valera, cotejada con diversas traducciones y revisada con arreglo á los originales hebreo y griego. Con referencias", Madrid, Depósito Central de la Sociedad Bíblica B. y E., 1911, printed by V. Tordesillas, 1912 (https://archive.org/details/lasantabibliaque00unse_0). John 3:9-18, Genesis 1:1-3, Psalm 23:1-3 and Revelation 22:20 read the same in both. In John 3:16 this text has "que ha dado á su Hijo unigénito, para que todo aquel que en él cree", where the older Valera text printed in New York in 1912 has "que haya dado ... creyere" (https://archive.org/details/lasantabibliaque00vale). The 1911 edition names no reviser: after its title page and table of books, Genesis begins.

Why it is public domain: the revision was published by 1911, before 1926, by an unnamed reviser. It is therefore an anonymous work and in the public domain everywhere. The people it names are the translators Casiodoro de Reina and Cipriano de Valera, whose translation (1569, revised 1602) dates from centuries before 1925. Valera is catalogued as "Valera, Cipriano de, 1532?-1625" (Princeton Theological Seminary Library record of the 1912 New York edition, https://archive.org/details/lasantabibliaque00vale). The revisers whom outside sources name, Juan Bautista Cabrera (died 18 May 1916) and Cipriano Tornos (died 30 November 1918) (https://www.literaturabautista.com/en-conmemoracion-del-primer-centenario-de-la-version-antigua-de-la-reina-valera-1909-2009/), also lived until 1925 or earlier. The committee that Spanish Wikisource says published a revision in 1923 (https://es.wikisource.org/wiki/Biblia_Reina-Valera_1909) cannot be the author of this text, because these words were already printed in 1911.

The read-aloud archive holds the Bible text chapter by chapter as plain text, a front file, the copyright page (copr.htm, left out of the source), and eBible.org's signing key (keys.asc, left out).

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page (https://ebible.org/details.php?id=spaRV1909), the edition's copyright page (https://ebible.org/spaRV1909/copyright.htm), https://es.wikisource.org/wiki/Biblia_Reina-Valera_1909.
